**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the failed-closure inventory test**

Adding this RESULT-0080 closure makes `scanFailedClosures()` return five result IDs, but `solver/tests/failedRunLedger.test.js:59-68` still hard-codes the previous four. I reproduced the resulting `LIVE: scanner reads the real retained failed closures` failure, which raises the full suite from the three documented deliberate failures to four and causes the new strict closeout check to fail. Update the inventory assertion, or derive it from the retained closure fixtures, before landing this row.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L47-L47](https://github.com/eluckey2002/Map-Elites-2248/blob/a49d3ab8578559fe318c2d7f82ecbef79a8ba13f/AGENTS.md#L47-L47)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Confirmed. The owner's frozen goal explicitly permits only new files under solver/tests/ and requires that no existing test be modified or skipped; it also says to stop and report when an item cannot be met. The full raw suite and strict close-out refusal already expose this fourth failure, and RESULT-0080 remains UNVERIFIED with no completed Path A-D. I am preserving both the required failed-run receipt and the existing assertion within that authorized scope. This PR must remain unmerged, as the owner requested. Updating the inventory test requires a separately authorized scope; the failure is not being waived or reported as passing.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the preregistration commit in the reviewed ancestry**

The closure records `e76f3ec4af2496495697322851bafca0ab73b253` as the immutable exploration-plan commit, but that commit and `f11ab98175305016a22a0aeadff82c165044d379` are siblings with the same parent rather than ancestor and descendant. Consequently, a clone containing only the reviewed history will not receive the recorded commit, `check-closeout.js` will fail when it runs `git show` on it, and the retained history no longer demonstrates that the plan preceded the games. Land the registration commit in reachable ancestry rather than squashing it away, and keep the recorded identity consistent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The pushed history retains the registration commit. Actual head a49d3ab8578559fe318c2d7f82ecbef79a8ba13f has e76f3ec4af2496495697322851bafca0ab73b253 as its direct parent. GitHub's compare API reports status=ahead, ahead_by=1, behind_by=0, and merge_base=e76f3ec (https://github.com/eluckey2002/Map-Elites-2248/compare/e76f3ec4af2496495697322851bafca0ab73b253...a49d3ab8578559fe318c2d7f82ecbef79a8ba13f). f11ab981 is not the pushed PR head. The registration was neither squashed nor replaced. I am adding an explicit reachable-ancestry/first-addition assertion and a negative test with an object-store sibling, alongside the raw GitHub comparison receipt.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist completed jobs before marking FR-0006 prevented**

If a worker or transport interruption occurs after some level jobs finish but before every job resolves, this `Promise.all` boundary again discards all completed responses because the panel is checkpointed only afterward, exactly reproducing FR-0006's recorded root cause. The named completion fence merely detects the incomplete artifact after the loss, and its test only mutates an in-memory fixture; it does not prevent recurrence despite the failed-run row being marked `PREVENTED`. Add atomic or per-job persistence with an interruption test, or leave the failure unprevented.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L96-L99](https://github.com/eluckey2002/Map-Elites-2248/blob/a49d3ab8578559fe318c2d7f82ecbef79a8ba13f/AGENTS.md#L96-L99)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Implemented in 9b31886 as solver/policy-lab/journaled-pool.js: each completed job is fsynced and atomically renamed before its promise resolves to the panel aggregate. The new test actually SIGKILLs a synthetic controller while its second job is in flight, verifies the first completed result survives, and refuses duplicate dispatch/journal reuse. FR-0006 now points to this prevention and its interruption test. The stopped run's controller, pool, worker and exploration plan are frozen by the owner's explicit rule, so they remain byte-identical; the new adapter is for a future preregistered harness, and no scientific games were rerun. The completion fence separately preserves the UNVERIFIED disposition. All 16 new tests pass; the full suite retains the disclosed four failures.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid opening journal directories as files on Windows**

On the owner's Windows checkout, `fs.openSync(path.dirname(file), 'r')` cannot open a directory with normal file flags and throws `EPERM`; because `atomicJson()` is used for the manifest, `createJournaledPool()` fails before it can launch a job (and both new journal tests are Linux-only in CI). Use a Windows-compatible directory durability path or conditionally skip the directory fsync while retaining the file fsync/rename behavior.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the parity panel's declared cells**

When a parity artifact contains duplicated, missing, or out-of-range cells (for example after a partial or corrupt aggregation), this `continue` bypasses both the completeness and declared-seed checks. `recompute.js:167-170` then checks only the trace-equality count and total, so even 200 copies of one cell can validate as 200/200 and back the ledger claim; validate these panels against the plan's exact 200 `(level, seed)` pairs instead of skipping them.
